The program established a strong foundation for commercialization of low-cost, non-flammable, long-duration zinc batteries for stationary storage. SUMMARY • Demonstrated Feasibility:– Thick MnO₂ cathodes with modified HEE delivered >100 mAh pouch cells.– Stainless steel current collectors + slurry coating identified as a cost-reduction pathway.– Bio-safe HE additive validated: suppresses HER, enhances Zn reversibility, effective in SO₄²⁻ electrolytes. • Remaining Challenges:– Thick cathode cycling stability and Zn dendrite suppression remain critical hurdles.– Scale-up of slurry processing and uniform electrode fabrication must be advanced.– Coupling cycle-life improvement with cost reduction is essential for market entry. • Path Forward:– Optimize MnO₂ morphology/architecture to balance stability and capacity.– Advance stainless steel current collector strategy to eliminate carbon paper dependency.– Integrate electrolyte additive strategy into scaled pouch cells for validation.– Leverage T2M modeling to align technical progress with commercialization timelines. • Year 2 Progress vs. Deliverables:– >100 mAh pouch cells achieved (capacity milestone).– Electrolyte development showed effective HER suppression and Zn reversibility.– <$30/kWh cost pathway demonstrated (Task 4.2 deliverable).– Commercialization milestones identified, positioned for Year 3. • Bottom Line:Year 2 established a strong foundation: pouch cells exceeded 100 mAh, electrolyte strategy validated, and <$30/kWh cost feasibility demonstrated. With cathode/electrolyte refinements, Zn anode stabilization, and T2M-guided scaling, the program is positioned to meet ARPA-E cost and cycle-life targets in the next phase. Appendix A.
